newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia ratifies EU accord, hails Commission move.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia ratifies EU accord, hails Commission move.

text.p: Slovenia ratified its association agreement with the European Union on Tuesday in a parliamentary vote coinciding with Brussels' decision to invite the ex-Yugoslav republic to begin full entry talks.

Parliament approved the association accord, signed in June 1996, by a vote of 70-3 at the end of a four-hour debate. The vote was a formality after parliamentary parties agreed on July 4 to press ahead with ratification by July 15.
"This is a very important, historic decision by parliament," Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek told reporters.
Earlier, the European Commission in Brussels agreed that Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovenia and Estonia should join Cyprus in entry talks for the EU's first expansion into Eastern Europe.
"The European Commission has made its decision known...(and) the chances for Slovenia (to join the EU in the first wave) have improved considerably," Drnovsek said.
"We are entering talks with a changed constitution and the association accord ratified," he continued.
Commision officals had said last week Slovenia would be invited to start talks on full EU membership early next year providing the country ratified its association accord immediately.
During the parliamentary debate opposition deputies accused the government of inadequately preparing laws to protect Slovenian national interests once it became an associate member.

The government overcame the last barrier to ratification on Monday when parliament voted to change the constitution to enable foreigners to buy land in line with provisions included in the association accord.
